instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Jos 5:4 died (H4191) stands in the explanation the reason introduces: the death of the generation that came out of Egypt is the cause of the new circumcision.
In Jam 3:17 sincere (G0505) closes the list of the qualities of wisdom that open to reason belongs to, seven places after it; they are joined only by the list.
In Num 18:32 bear (H5375J) opens the verse, two words before by reason of it: the giver will carry no sin, and the reason phrase gives why.
observations.grounds: you shall bear no sin by reason of it

observations.text: In 1Th 3:5 bear (G4722) stands two words after for this reason, in the clause of the cause: Paul could no longer endure not knowing, and so he sent.
observations.grounds: when I could bear it no longer

observations.text: In 1Ti 1:16 patience (G3115) stands nine words after for this reason, in the purpose it introduces: the mercy was given so that Christ's patience might be shown.
In 1Th 3:5 tempted (G3985G) stands eleven words after for this reason, in the fear that moved the sending: the cause of the sending includes the worry that the tempter had tempted them.
In Mar 12:24 wrong (G4105) stands directly after the reason: the reason is the cause of the error, and the error is named at once.
In Act 19:9 speaking evil (G2551) stands nine words before reasoning: the slander of the Way by some is part of what moved Paul to withdraw and reason elsewhere.
In Gen 47:13 languished (H3856A) stands directly before by reason of: the wasting of the land is the effect, and the famine named after it is the cause.
observations.grounds: languished by reason of the famine

observations.text: In Job 1:9 fear (H3372H) stands two words before for no reason: Satan's question asks whether Job's fear of God has no ground behind it; the fear is what the reason is questioned of.
observations.grounds: Does Job fear God for no reason

observations.text: In Act 24:25 alarmed (G1719) stands ten words after reasoned: Felix becomes afraid while Paul reasons about righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come; the alarm follows the content of the reasoning.
In Gen 41:31 plenty (H7647) opens the verse, three words before by reason of: the plenty is what will be forgotten, and the famine named after the reason phrase is why.
observations.grounds: the plenty will be unknown in the land

observations.text: In Dan 4:36 was established (H8627) stands fifteen words after reason, at the end of a sequence that begins with its return: reason, then glory, then the counselors' seeking, then the king set again in his kingdom.
observations.grounds: I was established in my kingdom

observations.text: In Gen 41:31 follow stands two words after by reason of and describes the famine it governs: the famine that comes after. The data gives the one English word three codes at the same place, H0310A (after), H1931 (it) and H3651C (so).
In 2Ti 1:6 remind (G0363) stands directly after for this reason, which governs it: the cause comes first and the reminder to rekindle the gift follows from it.
observations.grounds: For this reason I remind you

observations.text: In 1Ti 1:16 mercy (G1653) stands two words before for this reason, which gives its purpose: Paul received mercy, and the reason phrase opens why.
observations.grounds: I received mercy for this reason

observations.text: In Jam 3:17 mercy (G1656) stands two places after open to reason, the next quality in the list of the wisdom from above.
In Act 17:17 devout persons (G4576) are among those reasoned with: they stand five words after reasoned, joined to the Jews as the hearers in the synagogue.
observations.grounds: with the Jews and the devout persons

observations.text: In 1Pe 3:15 holy (G1161) stands eight words before reason, in the clause that comes first: Christ is set apart as holy in the heart before the readiness to give a reason.
observations.grounds: honor Christ the Lord as holy

observations.text: In Luk 9:47 hearts (G2588) stands two words after reasoning and names where the reasoning is: it is the reasoning of their hearts.
In 1Pe 3:15 hearts (G2588) opens the verse, eleven words before reason: the heart is where Christ is honored, and the reason is given outward to the one who asks.
In Dan 4:34 honored (H1922) stands six words after reason, among the acts of worship that follow its return.
In 1Pe 3:15 honor (G0037) and respect (G5401) frame the reason: Christ is honored in the heart before it, and the defense is made with respect after it.
In Act 28:20 hope (G1680) stands nine words after for this reason, in the clause that gives what Paul is bound for: the hope of Israel is why he wears the chain.
observations.grounds: because of the hope of Israel

observations.text: In 1Pe 3:15 hope (G1680) is what the reason is given for: it stands two words after reason, which accounts for it.
In Jam 3:17 impartial (G0087) stands six places after open to reason, in the same list of the qualities of the wisdom from above.
In Mar 12:24 know (G6063) stands two words after the reason and gives its content: they are wrong because they do not know the Scriptures nor God's power; the not knowing is the cause.
observations.grounds: because you know neither the Scriptures

observations.text: In Luk 9:47 knowing (G6063) stands directly before reasoning and takes it as its object: Jesus knows the reasoning of their hearts.
observations.grounds: knowing the reasoning of their hearts

observations.text: In 1Th 3:5 learn (G1097) stands six words after for this reason, in the purpose of the sending: Paul sent to learn about their faith. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through conclude, a synonym; the verses show know and learn instead.
observations.grounds: I sent to learn about your faith

observations.text: In 1Th 3:5 labor (G2873) stands fifteen words after for this reason, in the fear that moved the sending: that their labor among them would come to nothing.
observations.grounds: our labor would be in vain

observations.text: In 1Jo 3:8 works (G2041) is the object of the purpose the reason introduces: the devil's works are what the Son of God appeared to destroy.
In Dan 4:34 lives (H2417) stands seven words after reason and describes God, the one honored once reason returns: he lives forever; it is not joined to the reason.

In Dan 4:36 glory, majesty and splendor (H3367, H1923, H2122) return together with reason, joined to it by the same verb, and greatness (H7238) closes the verse: the return of reason opens the restoring of the king's rule.
observations.grounds: my majesty and splendor returned to me

observations.text: In Act 24:25 present (G3568) stands thirteen words after reasoned, in Felix's reply: he sends Paul away for now; the reasoning is cut short.
In Act 18:14 open (G0455) stands fifteen words before reason, in the opening clause: Paul was about to speak when Gallio answered; the reason is Gallio's, not Paul's.
In 1Th 3:5 vain (G2756) closes the verse, eighteen words after for this reason, in the fear that moved the sending: that the labor would be empty.
In Job 1:9 answered (H6030B) opens the verse, six words before for no reason: the question whether Job's fear has a cause is Satan's answer to the Lord.

In Pro 3:30 contend (H7378) stands two words before for no reason, which qualifies it: the strife forbidden is strife without cause. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through argue, a synonym; the verse pairs the reason with contend instead.
observations.grounds: Do not contend with a man for no reason

observations.text: In Jam 3:17 peaceable (G1516) stands two places before open to reason in the list of the qualities of the wisdom from above.
observations.grounds: then peaceable, gentle, open to reason

observations.text: In 1Pe 3:15 prepared (G2092) stands six words before reason: the readiness is to make a defense to the one who asks for the reason; the reason is what the believer is ready to give.
observations.grounds: always being prepared to make a defense

verses.text: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and sincere.
Do not contend with a man for no reason, when he has done you no harm.
But I received mercy for this reason, that in me, as the foremost, Jesus Christ might display his perfect patience as an example to those who were to believe in him for eternal life.
but in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; yet do it with gentleness and respect,
Then Satan answered the Lord and said, “Does Job fear God for no reason?
Whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the works of the devil.
And you shall bear no sin by reason of it, when you have contributed the best of it. But you shall not profane the holy things of the people of Israel, lest you die.’”
Jesus said to them, “Is this not the reason you are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “ If it were a matter of wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, I would have reason to accept your complaint.
And as he reasoned about righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix was alarmed and said, “ Go away for the present. When I get an opportunity I will summon you.”
For this reason, therefore, I have asked to see you and speak with you, since it is because of the hope of Israel that I am wearing this chain.”
And this is the reason why Joshua circumcised them: all the males of the people who came out of Egypt, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way after they had come out of Egypt.

At the same time my reason returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom, my majesty and splendor returned to me. My counselors and my lords sought me, and I was established in my kingdom, and still more greatness was added to me.
and the plenty will be unknown in the land by reason of the famine that will follow, for it will be very severe.

But when some became stubborn and continued in unbelief, speaking evil of the Way before the congregation, he withdrew from them and took the disciples with him, reasoning daily in the hall of Tyrannus.
For this reason, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to learn about your faith, for fear that somehow the tempter had tempted you and our labor would be in vain.
For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands,
So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.
Now there was no food in all the land, for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished by reason of the famine.
But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts, took a child and put him by his side

At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and praised and honored him who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom endures from generation to generation;
